fermentables.name: Fruity Pebbles
fermentables.description: Rice-based cereal that is nearly all sugar and gelatinised rice starch — hence a very high potential extract for a cereal. A pastry-sour and milkshake-IPA favourite.
fermentables.flavorNotes: Artificial fruit punch, sweet cereal milk.

fermentables.attribution: ppg is derived from the product's own Nutrition Facts panel as filed with USDA FoodData Central (Branded Foods, FDC ID 2626163, "PEBBLES SWEETENED RICE CEREAL (brand FRUITY PEBBLES)", Post Consumer Brands, LLC, published 31 August 2023): a 36 g serving declaring 31.0 g of total carbohydrate and 0.0 g of dietary fibre. This project's method is 46 x (total carbohydrate - fibre) / serving grams, so 46 x (31.0 - 0.0) / 36 = 39.6 - the stored 42.2 was high by 2.6. Branded Foods is label data supplied by the manufacturer, which for a packaged cereal is the primary statement of composition; the citation is the data endpoint rather than the portal page, which FDC serves from a client-side router and returns 404 to anything that is not a browser.
fermentables.sourceNote: The panel backs ppg and nothing else on this record. Colour in Lovibond and the maximum batch percentage are this project's own curation and are not sourced - no cereal manufacturer publishes either, because neither is a food-labelling quantity. Note also that ppg here is a ceiling and not a promise: the carbohydrate is mostly gelatinised starch, so it needs the diastatic power of a base malt to become fermentable, which is what requiresConversion records. fermentables.diastaticPowerNote: Unmalted starch. It has never been germinated, so it brings no meaningful amylase of its own and contributes nothing to the enzyme supply — every point of gravity it yields has to be converted by the diastatic power of the malt beside it. Recorded as zero rather than left blank precisely because it is not unknown: leaving it blank would let a 70%-corn bourbon mash look like a grist whose enzyme balance nobody could assess, when in fact it is the case the assessment exists for.
